the least squares covariance model parameters estimation is a difficult task.
the least squares collocation, using a proper covariance model, is a very powerful method of interpolation, which is not inferior to the other methods, such as kriging or inverse distance weighting.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LSC with the covariance parameters estimated with the least squares or ML methods is not reliable enough.
the covariance parameters estimation is not a simple task.
the covariance parameter N should be chosen in the range of the prediction error and not in a range of the data errors, as is sometimes suggested.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the covariance parameter N is more important for the LSC prediction than for the kriging.
the covariance parameters estimation error is not a negligible factor in the prediction accuracy.
a small error of the estimated covariance parameters may result in a big prediction error.
